mainEntity.name: How can I tell if bleeding around my implant is serious?

acceptedAnswer.text: Persistent bleeding that doesn't improve with gentle cleaning within a few days, especially when accompanied by swelling, pain, or discharge, may indicate developing peri-implant disease. Professional evaluation can determine whether the bleeding represents minor irritation or requires specific treatment.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the same oral hygiene routine for implants and natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whilst basic principles remain similar, implants often benefit from modified techniques. Softer brushing, specific floss types, and sometimes additional cleaning tools help maintain the delicate gum seal around implants without causing damage to the surrounding tissues.

mainEntity.name: Do dental implants bleed more easily than natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Healthy implants shouldn't bleed more easily than natural teeth. However, when inflammation develops, implant sites may show bleeding more readily because the gum attachment is typically thinner and more delicate than around natural teeth.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can implant problems develop compared to natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Peri-implant diseases often progress faster than periodontal diseases around natural teeth. Whilst natural periodontal problems may develop over months or years, implant complications can sometimes advance within weeks, making early detection and treatment particularly important.

mainEntity.name: What happens if implant bleeding is left untreated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Untreated inflammation around implants can progress to peri-implantitis, potentially causing bone loss and implant failure. Unlike natural teeth, implants cannot regenerate lost supporting tissues, making prevention and early treatment crucial for long-term success.

mainEntity.name: Should I stop cleaning around my implant if it bleeds?

acceptedAnswer.text: Continue gentle cleaning around bleeding implants, as bacterial accumulation will worsen the problem. Use softer techniques and seek professional guidance if bleeding persists. Stopping oral hygiene allows bacteria to multiply, potentially accelerating inflammatory processes.
